key_locators.content: Error-coordinate state space with Delta = [0, Delta_2, Delta_3, 0, Delta_5]^T; Delta_2, Delta_3 mismatched, Delta_5 matched.
FT-ISS definition and mu(t,tau) = (1+exp(-t/tau))/(2 exp(-t/tau)).
Coordinate change with C diverging at t -> t0+T; premise requires finite T.
E_2 dynamics contains (A_p/m) mu x_3 and mu Delta_2; this fixes the mu scaling.
x_3d prefactor is (A_p/m * mu)^-1, containing mu.
(9) second row has (A_p/m) x-tilde_3 without mu; (9) third row has 1/(mu V_0); (10) pressure term has no 1/mu. Pair leaves a residual.
Nominal control law with -x-tilde_4 + omega_nv^2(x-tilde_4+Phi_3), etc.
Delta-hat_i = -integral alpha_i sgn(e-dot_i + beta e_i^(q/p)) dt - beta e_i^(q/p).
Observer for x-hat_2, x-hat_3, x-hat_5; x_3 and x_4 are treated as measured.
V_i = s_i^2/2; s_i = e-dot_i + beta e_i^(q/p); (20) has -alpha_i sgn(s_i) - Delta-dot_i; (21) assumes |Delta-dot_i| < sigma_i.
The paper explicitly assumes x-double-dot-hat_i = x-double-dot_i.
FT-DOTC law uses -(Delta-hat_5 + Theta-bar_5) sgn(x-tilde_5).
(23) prefactor (A_p/m)^-1 without mu; (24) same pressure term as (10); (25)-(33) case analysis.
V-dot_5末项 indices all 5.
mu truncation at delta_t; |e-dot_i| <= |s_i| <= alpha_i^-1(sigma_i) as printed; gain conditions a1 > 1/tau, a2 > 1/tau - b/m.
m=440, piston area row symbol printed b (value 0.01 m^2), V0=0.004, rho=1e9, ke=0.49, omega_nv=152, epsilon_v=0.92, Ps=1e7.
Author reports position convergence 0.2 s and velocity 0.5 s; J_e = 454.3921 vs OFCDR 643.2316. These are author simulation values, not reproduced here.

old_review_corrections_adopted.correction: mu contains the design constant tau; mu-dot/mu in (1/(2 tau), 1/tau]; gain conditions a1 > 1/tau and a2 > 1/tau - b/m.
old_review_corrections_adopted.note: The printed symbol looks like a lowercase t/iota; I use tau for readability and note the notation difference.

old_review_corrections_adopted.correction: Sliding variable is s_i = e-dot_i + beta e_i^(q/p), not e_i + beta e_i^(q/p).
Equation (19) left side is V-dot_i, not an extra s_i factor; the original report's 'extra s_i' claim is withdrawn.
The theorem condition bounds |Delta-dot_i| < sigma_i, not |Delta_i| < sigma_i; Lemma 1 uses |Delta_i| < k_i separately.
Equation (35) bounds |e-dot_i|, not |e_i|; Theorem 2 Case 1 uses the estimate-error bound as if it were established.
old_review_corrections_adopted.extension: I additionally show that |e-dot_i| <= |s_i| is not universally true and give an algebraic counterexample.

old_review_corrections_adopted.correction: Table 1: omega_nv=152, ke=0.49, epsilon_v=0.92; the 'Piston area' row symbol is misprinted as b and should be A_p; viscous friction b value is not given.
Equation (8) prefactor contains mu; the earlier suspicion that 1/mu was missing is withdrawn.
Equation (31) indices are all 5; the 3/5 ambiguity is closed.
Theorem 1 gap is the author's explicit assumption x-double-dot-hat_i = x-double-dot_i, not a silently dropped linear term.
old_review_corrections_adopted.extension: I make precise that this is e-double-dot_i = 0 and that, combined with the Delta-hat-dot -> Delta-dot replacement, it forces e-dot_i = 0 on a non-generic manifold.

old_review_corrections_adopted.correction: mu bookkeeping is mutually inconsistent between (8)(25) and (9)(10)(23)(24).
old_review_corrections_adopted.note: I agree that mu is missing in the (A_p/m) terms. I do not agree that (9)(10)(11) are mutually self-consistent: on page 4, (9) third row has 1/(mu V_0), while (10) pressure term has 1/V_0, leaving the residual (2 rho A_p/V_0)(1 - 1/mu)(E-tilde_2 + Phi_1). This is a correction to the old report's O15 wording, not a reversal of its direction.

divergences_from_old_report.old_report: Said (9)(10)(11) are mutually self-consistent and (23)(24) are another self-consistent pair.
divergences_from_old_report.my_check: Visually, (9) third row contains 1/(mu V_0) but (10) pressure term does not; substituting (10) into (9) leaves a nonzero residual. The (A_p/m) channel is consistent as printed, but the pressure channel is not.
divergences_from_old_report.status: new correction to the old report

divergences_from_old_report.old_report: Wrote the effective decay rate as approximately c5 + 1/tau.
divergences_from_old_report.my_check: That rate only applies before the truncation at delta_t. After delta_t, mu is frozen at mu_max, so the long-term rate is c5; the 1/tau term is a transient effect.
Also, the chain |e-dot_i| = |Delta-hat_i - Delta_i| <= |s_i| uses zero drift and is not universally valid; explicit counterexample e=216, e-dot=-5, beta=1, q/p=1/3 gives |e-dot|=5 > |s|=1.

divergences_from_old_report.old_report: Said the condition depends on an unproven estimate-error bound.
divergences_from_old_report.my_check: In the worst sign branch (x-tilde_i < 0, Delta-hat_i = Delta_i = -D < 0), the residual is 2D - Theta-bar_i, so Theta-bar_i must exceed 2|Delta_i|, i.e. the disturbance magnitude, not just alpha_i^-1(sigma_i). This conflicts with the 'unknown upper bound' claim.

still_unverified: Author intent for the mu bookkeeping: which of (8)/(23) is the controller actually implemented, and whether the missing mu terms are typesetting errors. The page images show the inconsistency but cannot establish intent.
Numerical values of b, tau, alpha_i, beta, q/p, Theta-bar_i, delta_t, and observer/controller sampling time. Without them, neither (36) nor the author's simulation can be reproduced from Table 1.
Whether the Theorem 1 FTUB conclusion holds for the actual observer trajectories with the drift terms retained. No additional proof is supplied here.
Whether the Theorem 2 worst-sign branch can be closed with a constant Theta-bar_i that does not depend on the unknown disturbance bound.
Whether Delta_i is differentiable in the author's setting; (21) needs Delta-dot_i but the paper only states a Lipschitz-like condition.
Whether the closed-loop input u remains bounded; no sup|u| bound is proven, and saturation is explicitly future work.
Whether the noise simulation in Fig. 7 has any theorem-level guarantee; the theorem has no measurement-noise term.
The sign and magnitude of the spool bias v_e0, which affects whether Delta_5 can be negative and thus whether the worst-sign branch is physically reachable.
Pages 1-2 and 8-11 were not visually inspected as images; their content is from MinerU text only.
No simulation, code execution, or numerical reproduction was performed in this task.
